entries.title: Bulls coaching vacancy living up to the promise of casting a wide net
entries.summary: <p>Recently hired executive vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham made it sound like a wide net would be used for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls’</a> coaching search and that is proving to be the case.</p><p>The team has already been rumored to have a list of up-and-comers like San Antonio assistant Sean Sweeney, Minnesota’s Micah Nori, Oklahoma City’s Dave Bliss, former player Jerry Stackhouse, and even an in-house candidate in assistant Wes Unseld Jr. on the radar.</p><p>Miami assistant Chris Quinn is now in the mix, as the Bulls have reportedly received permission to talk to Quinn about the vacancy left when Billy Donovan opted to walk away from the head coaching seat after six seasons.</p><p>Quinn fits the job description that Graham laid out when he was hired, not only having a strong reputation for player development, but it doesn’t hurt that he’s worked under Erik Spoelstra — arguably one of the elite coaches in the league — since 2014.</p><p>Again, this remains a process for Graham, who may have to play the long game in a coaching hire with Bliss and Sweeney still involved in the Western Conference Finals.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Teen sets Kane County Cougars' bus ablaze in Winnipeg
entries.summary: <p>The Kane County Cougars’ bus was set on fire and destroyed early Thursday in Winnipeg, Manitoba, and a 15-year-old girl is facing charges related to arson. No one was hurt.</p><p>The Cougars, who were in town to play the Goldeyes in the American Association of Professional Baseball, were in their hotel when the teen allegedly set fire to the bus, which was engulfed in flames. Police arrived at the scene at around 1:50 a.m., and firefighters extinguished the blaze.</p><p>"Everyone is OK, and we are still determining if any gear or personal property was lost," Cougars vice president and general manager Curtis Haug told CBC News.</p><p>The Goldeyes helped the Cougars procure a bus to take them to Fargo, North Dakota, the next stop on their road trip. Windstar, the company whose bus was destroyed, will send a bus to Fargo to bring the Geneva-based Cougars home.</p><p>"We are very disappointed that this could happen to our family-owned company, and the loss of this vehicle will impact our business and operations," Windstar operations manager Jackson Greteman wrote in an email to CBC News, adding that the bus was worth $425,000.</p><p>"We are happy that no one was hurt in this reckless act of vandalism and are cooperating with local authorities."</p><p>Police at first took two teens into custody. The girl facing charges was released.<br></p>

entries.title: St. Patrick football star David Folorunsho commits to Notre Dame
entries.summary: <p>David Folorunsho grew up playing soccer in Nigeria.</p><p>Now he’s a centerpiece of Notre Dame football’s 2027 recruiting class.</p><p>It has been quite a journey for the St. Patrick junior.</p><p>“I’m blessed to be in this situation,” Folorunsho told the Sun-Time after announcing his commitment to Notre Dame on May 15 in a ceremony at St. Patrick. “I can’t put anything on me. I got to put it to Jesus Christ.”</p><p>A 6-3, 280-pound defensive lineman, Folorunsho is the consensus No. 2 player in Illinois in the 2027 cycle, the No. 3 defensive lineman nationally and the No. 43 player overall.</p><p>He moved from Nigeria to the United States when he was 11 and kept playing soccer for a few years. Then some friends invited him to football practice, and his athletic path was set.</p><p>He played offensive line before moving to the other side of the ball, a switch that suited him well.</p><p>What does he like about his current position?</p><p>“Just attacking, getting after the quarterback,” Folorunsho said. “I like to use my athleticism; that’s the main reason.”</p><p>Colleges have taken notice.</p><p>Folorunsho has more than 30 Power Four offers, including from Indiana, Ohio State, Alabama, Georgia, LSU, Miami, Michigan and Texas.</p><p>“David is a player with an unlimited upside,” national recruiting analyst Clint Cosgrove said. “He’s got a lot of physical talent. He’s still raw at this point, but as well as he’s still growing into his body, there’s a lot to like about him.</p><p>“He fires off the ball. . . . He’s a high, high motor kid.”</p><p>St. Patrick coach Tom Zbikowski, an All-America defensive back at Notre Dame before moving on to the NFL, said he didn’t steer Folorunsho to his alma mater.</p><p>“I kept it neutral,” Zbikowski told the Sun-Times. “I wanted him to do his own studying, take a real good look at all those programs. They’re all good programs — you’re not going to make a bad decision out of there.”</p><p>At the end of the process, though, Zbikowski said, “I think family . . . and him understanding that once football’s over that this is the best option for him and it can do the most for you, especially being from Chicago.</p><p>“It’s a different animal when you’re a Chicago kid that goes to Notre Dame.”</p><p>Academics were a major component of Folorunsho’s decision.</p><p>“I want to go for business marketing, and they have a great business school and great contacts to help me out with that,” he said.</p><p>Now Folorunsho can focus on his final season with the Shamrocks, who were 6-5 in Zbikowski’s first year.</p><p>“The main thing I’m going to emphasize is pad level and really shoot my hands, getting that knock-back [of] an O-lineman,” he said. “More pass-rush moves and just being more consistent with every rep.”</p><p>“He works every day in the morning, and he works every day after school,” Zbikowski said. “I think he loves the process of getting better every day.</p><p>“He loves football — really loves football. I know a lot of people play football, and they all want to be D1 until it’s time to be D1 and understand all that goes into it. I don’t think he’s going to shy away from that. In fact, I think that’s what’s going to bring the best out of him.<br></p>

entries.title: Northwestern women's lacrosse team beats Johns Hopkins to return to NCAA title game
entries.summary: <p>Madison Taylor and Maddie Epke scored four goals apiece, and Northwestern’s women’s lacrosse team beat Johns Hopkins 16-11 in the national semifinals Friday in Evanston to return to the NCAA championship game. The Wildcats will face North Carolina, which beat Maryland 16-6 in the first semifinal, at 11 a.m. Sunday at Martin Stadium.</p><p>Northwestern (17-3), the first school to host the women’s lacrosse championship outside the Eastern Time Zone, lost to the Tar Heels in the national final last year 12-8. The Cats are looking for their first national title since 2023 and ninth under coach Kelly Amonte Hiller.</p><p>Aditi Foster scored three goals, and Taylor Lapointe and Kate Ratanaproeksa had two each for the Wildcats, who outshot the Blue Jays 40-22. Ava Angello led the Blue Jays (17-4) with three goals.</p><p>Northwestern trailed 1-0, tied the score almost two minutes later and never trailed again. The Wildcats led 10-3 at halftime before the Blue Jays cut the deficit to three late in the third quarter. After Epke and Lapointe scored about a minute apart, the Blue Jays never got closer than within four again.<br></p>

entries.title: Rookie reliever Tyler Davis earning trust in White Sox' bullpen
entries.summary: <p>SAN FRANCISCO — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a> have had a line of relievers racking up frequent-flyer miles between Chicago and Triple-A Charlotte, but <b>Tyler Davis’</b> spot on the big-league charter should be secure if he keeps throwing the ball like he has over his first month in the majors.</p><p>Davis, who was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/23/white-sox-bryan-hudson-munetaka-murakami-tyler-davis" target="_blank" ><u>solely a position player</u></a> in his final college season and just started focusing exclusively on throwing a couple of years ago, contributed another shutdown inning in a combined Sox <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/05/19/white-sox-mariners-rally-meidroth-benintendi?55" target="_blank" ><u>one-hitter</u></a> Tuesday in Seattle. He arrived in San Francisco with a 3.09 ERA in 10 outings, nine of which were hitless, with eight walks and 11 strikeouts.</p><p>“He’s very competitive,” manager <b>Will Venable</b> said. “He’s got good stuff, and he’s not afraid to throw it in the zone. He’s a guy that really quickly earned trust here.”</p><p>Batters were hitting .091 against his fastball, which averages 96 mph.</p><p>“Just trusting myself, just trusting my ability and trusting what the catcher puts down and then having conviction in what I throw,” Davis said.</p><h3>Noah walking a fine line</h3><p>Rookie left-hander <b>Noah Schultz’s</b> start Monday against the Mariners marked his first big-league outing without issuing a walk.</p><p>“I did hit two guys, but no walks is definitely a step in the right direction,” Schultz said.</p><p>The walks had been the biggest problem over what has otherwise been a mostly promising rookie campaign for the Sox’ top pitching prospect, at 2-3 with a 4.93 ERA in seven starts (34⅔ innings) with 21 walks and 32 strikeouts.</p><p>Schultz, who’s scheduled to start Sunday against the Giants, said his latest focus is on “my posture. Making myself go straight to the plate, not doing too much being over-rotational.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a home runs this season, two apiece from veteran outfielders <b>Derek Hill</b> and <b>Randal Grichuk</b>, who went deep in the ninth inning of the Sox’ 5-4 loss at Seattle.</p><p>It’s another area the Sox have turned around early this season, slashing .240/.397/.560 in 50 pinch-hitting at-bats. Sox pinch hitters went an anemic .134/.216/.157 last season without a homer.</p><p>“I love it,” Hills said of his late-game opportunities. “It’s an absolute blessing to be even considered to go up there and execute in that position, so I don’t take it lightly.”</p><h3>Injuries in the outfield</h3><p>Left fielder <b>Austin Hays</b> (calf strain) progressed well through his first three games of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/05/04/white-sox-sign-outfielder-randal-grichuk-put-outfielder-austin-hays-on-injured-list" target="_blank" ><u>a rehab assignment</u></a> this week at Charlotte and will be reevaluated after playing another series this weekend, Venable said.</p><p>The timetable is less clear for outfielder <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/21/everson-pereira-white-sox-outfield" target="_blank" ><b><u>Everson Pereira</u></b></a>, who is swinging but hasn’t thrown at full speed since a shoulder injury landed him on the injured list April 29. “I didn’t expect this to linger for this long,” Pereira said through interpreter <b>Billy Russo</b>.</p><p>It all leaves outfield roster questions, with <b>Sam Antonacci</b> entrenching himself in left and <b>Tristan Peters</b> holding down in center.</p><p>“We’ve still got a few days before Austin comes back, and we’ll see what happens between then and now,” Venable said. “Really good problems to have, when you have a lot of guys on your roster that are doing a really good job on a daily basis.”</p><p><b>Jarred Kelenic</b>, who has logged regular playing time in right field this month, was a late scratch Friday after getting hit in the lower back by a ball during the Giants’ batting practice. entries.title: Dr. Olusimbo Ige out as Chicago health chief
entries.summary: <p>Chicago Department of Public Health Commissioner Dr. Olusimbo Ige has resigned from her position, the mayor’s office confirmed Friday.</p><p>Fikirte Wagaw, the CDPH first deputy commissioner, will serve as acting commissioner, according to a spokesperson for Mayor Brandon Johnson’s office, who added that the mayor “will work expeditiously to identify a permanent replacement.”</p><p>A source familiar with the matter confirmed Friday that Johnson had asked for Ige's resignation, which is effective immediately.</p><p>“Today, Mayor Johnson accepted Dr. Ige’s letter of resignation. We thank her for her expertise and years of service as Commissioner for the Chicago Department of Public Health (CDPH),” a spokesperson for the mayor’s office said in a statement.</p><p>Ige is a public health expert — trained in medicine in Nigeria, where she grew up, and not licensed to practice in the U.S. Before taking the Chicago job, she worked for the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. Before that, she served as an assistant commissioner at New York City’s health department.</p><p>Johnson chose her from among four finalists produced by a nationwide search led by a committee that included former Illinois Department of Public Health Director Dr. Ngozi Ezike; Dr. Wayne H. Giles, dean of the School of Public Health at the University of Illinois at Chicago; Dr. David Ansell, a high-ranking official at Rush University Medical Center; and Arturo Carrillo, who at the time was deputy director for health and violence prevention at the Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.</p><p>Carrillo is now the city's deputy mayor for health and human services. Reached by the Sun-Times Friday evening, he had no comment on Ige's departure. </p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2023/11/13/23958969/mayor-brandon-johnson-chooses-chicago-health-commissioner-olusimbo-ige-replace-allison-arwady" target="_blank" >Ige was announced</a> as public health commissioner by Johnson in November 2023 just months after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2023/8/11/23827860/chicago-public-health-chief-dr-allison-arwady-brandon-johnson-lightfoot" target="_blank" >the mayor fired Dr. Allison Arwady</a>, a pediatrician and infectious diseases expert who led the city through the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/coronavirus" target="_blank" >COVID-19 pandemic</a>.</p><p>Arwady also had clashed with the Chicago Teachers Union for opening Chicago Public Schools during the pandemic earlier than the union wanted them to open without the protections the CTU had demanded.</p><p>Arwady's firing came as no surprise. Johnson was a paid organizer of the CTU who owed his election to the millions of dollars contributed by the union and the hundreds of foot soldiers the group and its affiliates provided.</p><p>Like Ige, Arwady was fired late on a Friday.<br></p>
